source: Numbers saved at export time (export-v1.1 full run) and from eval-final-v2 / probe-v2 on the TEST split. Replace this file with the eval-final-v4 results and rebuild to refresh the tab.

sections.title: This export, on the TEST split (1,001 studies)
sections.note: CE14 / CE5: CheXbert clinical-efficacy F1 of the generated impression against the reference, over all 14 labels / the 5 most common findings. Measured with the exported ONNX models on a Kaggle CPU.
rows: fp32 and fp16-storage decoders give identical reports
identical to the fp32 reference on 100% of the TEST reports

sections.title: Student against its 3B teacher (TEST)
sections.note: Student = this model (K10s1_fb2, about 95M parameters). Teacher = CheXagent-2-3b. RadCliQ: lower is better.
rows: student vs teacher; the student is slightly worse here

sections.title: Screening flags and the text (TEST, five common findings)
sections.note: Pooled over Cardiomegaly, Edema, Consolidation, Atelectasis and Pleural Effusion. Flags are tuned for about 90% sensitivity on validation.
rows: 90% of studies without findings get at least one flag
a safety net, not a triage tool

sections.title: Compression of the decoder (TEST, paired against fp32)
sections.note: Only the fp16-storage decoder passed the pre-registered check, so it is the one in the app.
rows: fails: generation collapses (97.5% hit the length cap)

sections.title: How to read these numbers
sections.note: The app is a draft-report assistant, not a diagnostic device. The student writes the common findings well; the report text never names 7 of the 10 flagged findings, which are rare in the training data.
